title: apps/console: the `vendor-objectstack` advancedChunks group folds the lazily-imported `@objectstack/lint` into an eagerly-loaded chunk — 89 KiB gzipped on every page load
body:
Filed from objectstack-ai/objectstack#9707, the framework-side measurement card. That card measured the cost; this is where the cause lives. **The fix is one line in `apps/console/vite.config.ts`, and I verified it by building the console with the change applied** — numbers below.

Not assigned to anyone. No PR opened from the framework side.

## What happens

`packages/app-shell/src/preview/capabilityLint.ts` imports the linter lazily and deliberately:

```ts
const mod: any = await import('@objectstack/lint');
```

It feature-detects exactly one export, `validateCapabilityReferences`, and runs it as a pre-publish advisory pass in the metadata designer. That is the **only** runtime reference to `@objectstack/lint` anywhere in this repo — I checked every occurrence at the pinned SHA; the rest are prose in comments and one line in `packages/app-shell/package.json`. So there is no second, static import defeating the lazy one.

The lazy import nonetheless buys nothing, because of this group in `apps/console/vite.config.ts`:

```js
const VENDOR_OBJECTSTACK_TEST = /([\\/]node_modules[\\/]@objectstack[\\/]|[\\/]@objectstack\+)/;
// ...
{ name: 'vendor-objectstack', test: vendorObjectstackTest, priority: 95 },
```

The test matches **every** `@objectstack/*` package, so `@objectstack/lint` is forced into the same chunk as `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/client`. Those two are reached synchronously from the app entry, so the group's chunk is a **static** import of `index-*.js` — which `index.html` loads. Rolldown honours the group over the module's async-only reachability, and the linter becomes eager. 17 chunks statically import `vendor-objectstack`; the entry chunk is one of them.

This is not a stale-copy or an injection problem — it is true of the published lint package, and it is chunk placement only.

## Measured

Build provenance: framework `main` @ `6f40ed736`, objectui pin `82a94170c405`, `scripts/build-console.sh` unmodified, visualizer and compression plugins active (CI unset).

Baseline:

| | raw | gzip |
|---|---|---|
| `vendor-objectstack-DEHi9gWK.js` (largest chunk in the app) | 5,783,887 | 1,759,970 |
| entire eager closure — 59 chunks reachable by static import from `index.html` | 14,157,562 | 4,117,647 |
| `@objectstack/lint` `dist/index.js` as installed | 532,262 | — |

Every console page load downloads and parses the whole linter.

## The fix, and what it is worth

Exclude lint from the group so it falls back to the async chunk its dynamic import already implies:

```js
const VENDOR_OBJECTSTACK_TEST =
  /([\\/]node_modules[\\/]@objectstack[\\/](?!lint[\\/])|[\\/]@objectstack\+(?!lint@))/;
```

Both alternatives need the lookahead: under pnpm the module resolves through a path that matches each of them. I applied exactly this, rebuilt the console, and measured:

| | baseline | with the fix | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| eager closure, gzipped | 4,117,647 | 4,026,464 | **−91,183 (−89.0 KiB)** |
| eager closure, raw | 14,157,562 | 13,861,026 | −296,536 |
| eager chunk count | 59 | 59 | 0 |

The linter relocates to its own chunk (`dist-*.js`, 294,800 raw / 91,155 gzipped) which is **not** in the eager closure — it is fetched only when an author publishes in the metadata designer, which is what the `await import` was always asking for. Nothing else moved: the chunk count is unchanged and the emitted asset count is 507 both times.

**89 KiB gzipped off every single page load, for a one-line regex change.**

## Two things worth knowing before someone tries a different fix

1. **Swapping the import to `@objectstack/lint/runtime` is not a fix.** That subpath advertises itself as the kernel-safe light entry, but its module graph reaches 70 of the 72 modules the main entry reaches, and on disk it is 498,225 bytes against the main entry's 532,262 — 93.6%. It also does not export `validateCapabilityReferences` at all.
2. **The three browser-externalization warnings naming lint (`module`, `path`, `fs`) are a symptom, not the cost.** The linter reaches `sucrase` and `typescript` through `createRequire` at call time and that code is never on the console's path, so the heavy transpilers are not bundled. I confirmed the warnings are lint's by replacing its entry with a stub: the build's externalization warnings went from 4 to 1, and the survivor is unrelated. Removing those imports from the framework package would not move the bytes.

## Refs

- objectstack-ai/objectstack#9707 — the framework-side measurement card this came from, which also carries the verdict on whether a framework-side export-map change is warranted (it is not required to capture the win above).
- objectstack-ai/objectstack#9659 — the measurement round that produced #9707.
